method: Ten statements per axis, five pointing each way; answers −2 to +2; axis = 50 + 50 × mean(answer × direction) / 2.

questions.statement: Student suicides in coaching hubs like Kota show the state must provide free mental-health care in every school and college.
questions.context: The Mental Healthcare Act 2017 made mental-health care a right; Kota recorded more than two dozen student suicides in 2023.
questions.ifAgree: Counsellors, helplines and limits on coaching hours, as in the 2024 coaching guidelines.
questions.ifDisagree: Families and institutions, not the state, should carry this responsibility.

questions.statement: India should give shelter to anyone fleeing persecution, whatever their religion.
questions.context: India sheltered Tibetans from 1959 and Sri Lankan Tamils from the 1980s.
questions.ifAgree: India’s tradition is “atithi devo bhava” — the guest is God.
questions.ifDisagree: Compassion must not endanger national security.

questions.statement: India was right to stay out of the RCEP trade pact in 2019.
questions.context: India walked out of the 15-nation Asia-Pacific trade deal in November 2019, fearing a flood of Chinese imports.
questions.ifAgree: Farmers, dairy and small industry were protected.
questions.ifDisagree: India missed a chance to join Asian supply chains.

questions.statement: It should be easier for companies to hire and fire workers.
questions.context: India merged 29 labour laws into four labour codes, passed in 2019–20.
questions.ifAgree: Employers argue rigid rules keep factories small and workers informal.
questions.ifDisagree: Unions say looser rules weaken job security and the right to strike.

questions.statement: Most subsidies on food, fertiliser and fuel should be phased out to cut the deficit.
questions.context: Food and fertiliser subsidies cost the centre several lakh crore rupees a year.
questions.ifAgree: Targeted cash or nothing, not open-ended subsidies.
questions.ifDisagree: Cutting fertiliser subsidies would hurt small farmers.

questions.statement: Foreign governments and UN bodies have no business commenting on Kashmir or Manipur.
questions.context: India rejects third-party mediation on Kashmir under the 1972 Simla Agreement.
questions.ifAgree: These are internal matters.
questions.ifDisagree: Human rights are a universal concern.

questions.statement: Linking rivers is worth the ecological risk.
questions.context: The Ken–Betwa link, approved in 2021, will submerge part of the Panna Tiger Reserve.
questions.ifAgree: It would bring water to drought-hit Bundelkhand.
questions.ifDisagree: It destroys forests and tiger habitat.

questions.statement: Rohingya refugees should be deported, not sheltered.
questions.context: India has not signed the 1951 Refugee Convention; the Supreme Court allowed deportations in 2021.
questions.ifAgree: India must put its own security and people first, whatever the sympathy.
questions.ifDisagree: Sending refugees back to persecution in Myanmar is wrong.

questions.statement: High import duties on electronics, cars and farm goods protect Indian jobs.
questions.context: India has some of the highest tariffs of any large economy, especially on cars and farm goods.
questions.ifAgree: Duties helped bring phone assembly to India.
questions.ifDisagree: Tariffs make goods dearer and Indian firms less competitive.

questions.statement: Shops on pilgrimage routes should not be forced to display their owners’ names.
questions.context: Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand ordered nameplates on the Kanwar Yatra route in 2024; the Supreme Court stayed the orders.
questions.ifAgree: It invites boycotts of Muslim shopkeepers.
questions.ifDisagree: Pilgrims have a right to know where their food comes from.

questions.statement: Politicians should not use temples, mosques or religious symbols in election campaigns.
questions.context: The Supreme Court held in 2017 that appealing for votes on grounds of religion is a corrupt practice.
questions.ifAgree: Religion should stay out of the ballot box.
questions.ifDisagree: Faith is part of public life and voters’ identity.

questions.statement: AFSPA, which shields soldiers from prosecution in “disturbed areas”, should be repealed.
questions.context: Repeal was demanded again after 14 civilians were killed by soldiers in Nagaland in December 2021.
questions.ifAgree: Irom Sharmila fasted for 16 years against it.
questions.ifDisagree: Troops need legal protection in insurgencies.

questions.statement: India should revive regional cooperation through SAARC with all its neighbours.
questions.context: SAARC summits have stalled since India boycotted the 2016 Islamabad summit.
questions.ifAgree: South Asia is among the least integrated regions in the world.
questions.ifDisagree: No regional forum with Pakistan while it shelters terrorists.

questions.statement: Suspending the Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan was justified.
questions.context: India put the 1960 treaty “in abeyance” in April 2025.
questions.ifAgree: “blood and water cannot flow together.”
questions.ifDisagree: Water should never be used as a weapon.

questions.statement: Adults should be free to watch any film or series without state certification.
questions.context: OTT platforms were brought under a government code of ethics by the IT Rules of 2021.
questions.ifAgree: Adults can decide for themselves; age ratings are enough.
questions.ifDisagree: Shows like Tandav (2021) drew cases for hurting religious sentiments.

questions.statement: The censor board should cut scenes that hurt religious sentiments.
questions.context: The CBFC certifies every film for cinemas; Padmaavat (2018) was renamed and edited after protests.
questions.ifAgree: The cuts demanded in Padmaavat or PK.
questions.ifDisagree: The Supreme Court said in the Padmaavat case that states cannot ban a certified film.

questions.statement: Young Indians should work 70 hours a week to build the country, as Narayana Murthy urged.
questions.context: The Infosys founder’s 2023 remark set off a national debate about work and burnout.
questions.ifAgree: China and Japan grew on punishing work hours.
questions.ifDisagree: Long hours harm health and productivity; labour law sets 48 hours a week.

questions.statement: Sedition-style laws should be scrapped completely, including the new provision on “endangering sovereignty”.
questions.context: The colonial sedition law was suspended by the Supreme Court in 2022; Section 152 of the 2023 penal code replaced it.
questions.ifAgree: Such laws have been used against students, journalists and protesters.
questions.ifDisagree: The state needs a law against those who incite secession.

questions.statement: Panchayats and city councils should control their own budgets and services.
questions.context: The 73rd and 74th amendments of 1992 created local self-government, but most money is still controlled by states.
questions.ifAgree: Kerala’s “people’s plan” giving 35–40% of plan funds to local bodies.
questions.ifDisagree: Local bodies lack capacity and invite local capture.

questions.statement: Governors should not be able to sit on bills passed by elected state assemblies.
questions.context: Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Punjab took their governors to the Supreme Court over long-delayed assent.
questions.ifAgree: An appointed governor should not block an elected assembly.
questions.ifDisagree: Governors are a constitutional check on states.

questions.statement: Manipur’s conflict needs political talks, not just more troops.
questions.context: Violence between Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities since May 2023 has killed more than 250 people; President’s Rule was imposed in 2025.
questions.ifAgree: Only a political settlement can end the conflict.
questions.ifDisagree: Order must be restored first.

questions.statement: The Places of Worship Act, which freezes the religious character of sites as of 1947, must be enforced: no more temple–mosque suits.
questions.context: Suits over the Gyanvapi mosque in Varanasi and the Shahi Idgah in Mathura test the 1991 law.
questions.ifAgree: Reopening history invites endless conflict.
questions.ifDisagree: Hindus have a right to reclaim sites they say were destroyed.

questions.statement: India should accept international human-rights scrutiny like any democracy.
questions.context: India has rejected criticism from UN rapporteurs and foreign governments as interference.
questions.ifAgree: A confident democracy has nothing to hide.
questions.ifDisagree: Such criticism is often selective and political.

questions.statement: Indians should buy Indian goods even when they cost more — “vocal for local”.
questions.context: Modi launched the Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) campaign in 2020.
questions.ifAgree: Patanjali’s swadeshi marketing or Khadi.
questions.ifDisagree: Consumers should buy what is best value, wherever it is made.

questions.statement: People should rely on family and savings, not the government, in old age.
questions.context: Most elderly Indians depend on their children; only a minority have a pension.
questions.ifAgree: The joint family is India’s real safety net.
questions.ifDisagree: Universal old-age pensions are needed as families shrink and migrate.

questions.statement: Films and web series show too much sex and swearing and should tone it down.
questions.context: Shows like Sacred Games and Mirzapur drove complaints that led to the 2021 OTT rules.
questions.ifAgree: What families watch together should reflect Indian values.
questions.ifDisagree: Adults can choose; creators should not be policed for language.

questions.statement: Indian and Pakistani artists and cricketers should be free to work together.
questions.context: Pakistani actors were effectively barred from Indian films after 2016; there has been no bilateral cricket series since 2012–13.
questions.ifAgree: Culture and sport build peace between peoples.
questions.ifDisagree: No normal ties while terror continues.

questions.statement: India should not accept international climate targets that limit its growth.
questions.context: At COP26 India pledged net zero by 2070 and pushed to “phase down” rather than “phase out” coal.
questions.ifAgree: Rich countries polluted first and should cut first.
questions.ifDisagree: India is among the most climate-vulnerable countries.

questions.statement: Textbooks should teach more about Indian achievements and less about the Mughals.
questions.context: NCERT removed a chapter on the Mughal courts from its Class 12 history book in 2023.
questions.ifAgree: Indian history should centre Indian kingdoms and heroes.
questions.ifDisagree: History should be taught whole, including uncomfortable parts.

questions.statement: Women of all ages should be allowed into every temple, including Sabarimala.
questions.context: The Supreme Court lifted the ban on women aged 10–50 in 2018; review petitions went to a larger bench.
questions.ifAgree: Equal access is a constitutional right.
questions.ifDisagree: Devotees say the deity’s celibate form is a matter of faith.

questions.statement: No prime minister should serve more than two terms.
questions.context: India has no term limits; Nehru served 17 years and Modi began a third term in 2024.
questions.ifAgree: Limits stop any leader dominating institutions.
questions.ifDisagree: Voters should decide how long a leader serves.

questions.statement: India’s growing number of billionaires is a sign of success, not a problem.
questions.context: India has around 200 billionaires on the Forbes list, third only to the US and China.
questions.ifAgree: Wealth creators like Infosys or Reliance build jobs and tax revenue.
questions.ifDisagree: The World Inequality Lab says the top 1% hold about 40% of India’s wealth.

questions.statement: Mountain highways like the Char Dham road should be scaled back to protect the Himalayas.
questions.context: The 2023 Silkyara tunnel collapse on the project trapped 41 workers for 17 days; Joshimath was sinking the same year.
questions.ifAgree: The Himalayas are young, fragile mountains.
questions.ifDisagree: Hill states need roads for pilgrims, the army and jobs.

questions.statement: Free grain for 80 crore people should continue as long as it is needed.
questions.context: Under the PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, 5 kg of free grain a month was extended in 2024 for five years.
questions.ifAgree: Food security kept millions fed through the pandemic.
questions.ifDisagree: Critics ask why a fast-growing economy still needs free grain for most of its people.

questions.statement: A legal guarantee of paid rural work, like MGNREGA’s 100 days, is essential.
questions.context: The 2005 law guaranteed up to 100 days of wage work a year to every rural household that asks.
questions.ifAgree: It was a lifeline when migrant workers walked home in the 2020 lockdown.
questions.ifDisagree: Critics call it a leaky make-work scheme that creates few lasting assets.

questions.statement: India should cut its own tariffs rather than retaliate against US tariffs.
questions.context: The US imposed tariffs of up to 50% on many Indian goods in August 2025, partly over India’s Russian oil purchases.
questions.ifAgree: Lower Indian tariffs could unlock a trade deal.
questions.ifDisagree: India should stand firm and protect farmers and dairy.

questions.statement: The anti-terror law UAPA is necessary, even if accused people stay in jail for years before trial.
questions.context: Bail is very hard to get under UAPA; several people arrested in the 2020 Delhi riots “conspiracy” case were held for years without trial.
questions.ifAgree: Terror cases need tough laws to protect national security.
questions.ifDisagree: “bail is the rule, jail the exception”, as the Supreme Court has said.

questions.statement: India should stop building new coal power plants.
questions.context: Coal still generates about three-quarters of India’s electricity.
questions.ifAgree: Solar is now cheaper than new coal.
questions.ifDisagree: Coal is reliable and employs millions.

questions.statement: India should work through the UN and other global bodies, and win a permanent Security Council seat by building coalitions.
questions.context: India has sought a permanent seat for decades with the G4 (Brazil, Germany, Japan).
questions.ifAgree: Global rules protect a rising middle power.
questions.ifDisagree: The UN is outdated and India should act alone when needed.

questions.statement: Internet shutdowns are justified to stop riots and rumours.
questions.context: India orders more shutdowns than any other country; Kashmir’s began in August 2019 and 4G returned only in February 2021.
questions.ifAgree: Shutdowns stop rumours spreading on WhatsApp during riots.
questions.ifDisagree: The Supreme Court held in 2020 that indefinite shutdowns are unconstitutional.

questions.statement: States should get a bigger share of the taxes they raise.
questions.context: The Finance Commission gives states 41% of the divisible pool; southern states say they get back far less than they pay.
questions.ifAgree: Richer states fund the union but have little say over the money.
questions.ifDisagree: Redistribution to poorer states keeps the union fair.

questions.statement: Cheap petrol and diesel matter more than green taxes.
questions.context: Fuel taxes make up a large share of pump prices.
questions.ifAgree: Fuel prices drive inflation for the poor.
questions.ifDisagree: Green taxes fund clean transport.

questions.statement: Sex education should be taught in every school.
questions.context: Several states halted the Adolescence Education Programme in 2007 after objections.
questions.ifAgree: It protects children from abuse and myths.
questions.ifDisagree: It is a matter for parents.

questions.statement: India should keep its pledge never to use nuclear weapons first.
questions.context: India’s 2003 nuclear doctrine pledges no first use; the Defence Minister said in 2019 that this could change.
questions.ifAgree: It makes India a responsible nuclear power.
questions.ifDisagree: Ambiguity deters Pakistan better.

questions.statement: The super-rich should pay a wealth or inheritance tax.
questions.context: India abolished estate duty in 1985 and the wealth tax in 2015.
questions.ifAgree: The World Inequality Lab’s 2024 proposal of a 2% tax on fortunes above ₹10 crore.
questions.ifDisagree: Sam Pitroda’s 2024 remark on inheritance tax drew a backlash and the Congress distanced itself.

questions.statement: Banks, coal and other key sectors should stay in government hands.
questions.context: Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 banks in 1969 and the coal industry in 1971–73.
questions.ifAgree: Public banks like SBI lend to farmers and remote areas private banks ignore.
questions.ifDisagree: Public banks carried most of the bad loans uncovered after 2015.

questions.statement: The Emergency of 1975–77 brought discipline that India needed.
questions.context: Indira Gandhi suspended civil liberties and elections for 21 months; the press was censored and opponents jailed.
questions.ifAgree: Trains ran on time and strikes stopped, its defenders said.
questions.ifDisagree: Forced sterilisations, jailed opponents and a censored press.

questions.statement: India should keep talking to Pakistan, even after terror attacks.
questions.context: Vajpayee took a bus to Lahore in 1999; Modi visited Lahore in 2015.
questions.ifAgree: Dialogue is the only lasting path to peace.
questions.ifDisagree: “terror and talks cannot go together.”

questions.statement: Election commissioners should be chosen by a panel that includes the Chief Justice, not by the government alone.
questions.context: A 2023 law replaced the Chief Justice on the selection panel with a Union minister.
questions.ifAgree: A neutral referee needs independent appointment.
questions.ifDisagree: Appointments are an executive function in a parliamentary system.

questions.statement: Foreign funding of NGOs should be tightly controlled.
questions.context: Amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act in 2020 tightened rules; thousands of NGOs have lost their licences.
questions.ifAgree: Foreign money should not shape Indian politics.
questions.ifDisagree: It chokes charities, research and rights groups.

questions.statement: Journalists should be free to criticise the government without fear of raids or arrest.
questions.context: NewsClick’s founder was arrested under UAPA in 2023; India ranks in the bottom third of RSF’s press-freedom index.
questions.ifAgree: A free press is how voters learn what power is doing.
questions.ifDisagree: Some outlets spread propaganda and foreign-funded agendas.

questions.statement: Delhi’s air pollution is an emergency that justifies banning old vehicles and firecrackers.
questions.context: Delhi bars diesel vehicles over 10 years old and petrol over 15; the Supreme Court has repeatedly restricted firecrackers.
questions.ifAgree: Polluted air shortens millions of lives.
questions.ifDisagree: Bans fall hardest on the poor and on festivals.

questions.statement: The 2020 farm laws, which let farmers sell outside government mandis, were good reform.
questions.context: Passed in September 2020, the laws were repealed in November 2021 after a year-long protest on Delhi’s borders.
questions.ifAgree: Economists who backed them said private buyers and contract farming would raise farmers’ incomes.
questions.ifDisagree: Farm unions feared the end of assured government procurement and corporate control of agriculture.

questions.statement: Free electricity, water and bus rides promised before elections damage state finances.
questions.context: PM Modi criticised “revdi culture” in 2022; free power and bus travel became standard promises of many parties.
questions.ifAgree: Several states borrow heavily to fund subsidies.
questions.ifDisagree: Free power or bus travel is welfare for the poor, not a giveaway.

questions.statement: Long sit-ins like Shaheen Bagh or the farmers’ protest are legitimate even if they block roads for months.
questions.context: The Supreme Court ruled in 2020 that public roads cannot be occupied indefinitely.
questions.ifAgree: Peaceful, sustained protest forced the repeal of the farm laws.
questions.ifDisagree: Commuters and businesses should not pay the price of protest.

questions.statement: Environmental clearances slow down development and should be faster.
questions.context: The 2023 Forest Conservation Amendment eased rules for projects near borders.
questions.ifAgree: Delays raise costs and stall jobs.
questions.ifDisagree: Rushed clearances lead to disasters.

questions.statement: Arrests of opposition leaders by central agencies before elections threaten democracy.
questions.context: Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal and Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren were arrested by the ED in 2024; both later got bail.
questions.ifAgree: Opposition parties say the ED and CBI are used selectively.
questions.ifDisagree: No one is above the law, chief ministers included.

questions.statement: Transgender people should have reservations in jobs and education.
questions.context: The Supreme Court recognised a third gender in 2014 (NALSA) and asked for reservations; Karnataka offers 1%.
questions.ifAgree: Trans people face exclusion from school and work.
questions.ifDisagree: Reservations should remain for caste-based disadvantage.

questions.statement: Big projects like the Great Nicobar port should stop if they destroy rainforest and tribal land.
questions.context: The ₹72,000 crore project would clear about 130 sq km of forest on an island home to the Shompen people.
questions.ifAgree: Some forests and peoples cannot be replaced.
questions.ifDisagree: India needs strategic ports and growth in the Indian Ocean.

questions.statement: One tax for the whole country, GST, was worth states giving up their own taxes.
questions.context: Launched in July 2017 and run jointly by the centre and states through the GST Council; rates were cut to mainly two slabs in 2025.
questions.ifAgree: One market, fewer checkpoints and less evasion.
questions.ifDisagree: States lost fiscal freedom and wait for compensation.

questions.statement: Live-in couples should have to register with the authorities, as in Uttarakhand.
questions.context: Uttarakhand’s Uniform Civil Code, in force since January 2025, requires live-in relationships to be registered.
questions.ifAgree: Registration protects women and children in such relationships.
questions.ifDisagree: It intrudes on adults’ privacy.

questions.statement: Celebrities and students who criticise India abroad are anti-national.
questions.context: “Anti-national” became a common charge after the 2016 JNU sedition case.
questions.ifAgree: Dirty linen should not be washed in foreign media.
questions.ifDisagree: Criticising the government is not criticising India.

questions.statement: Demolishing the homes of people accused of rioting is fair and fast justice.
questions.context: The Supreme Court ruled in November 2024 that punitive demolitions without due process are unconstitutional.
questions.ifAgree: The “bulldozer” demolitions in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.
questions.ifDisagree: Punishment must follow trial, and families should not lose homes for an accusation.

questions.statement: Films made tax-free by governments, like The Kashmir Files, are propaganda.
questions.context: Several BJP-ruled states made The Kashmir Files (2022) tax-free; West Bengal banned The Kerala Story (2023) until the Supreme Court stayed the ban.
questions.ifAgree: Governments should not promote films with a political message.
questions.ifDisagree: These films tell stories of suffering that were long ignored.

questions.statement: The death penalty should be abolished, even for terrorists.
questions.context: India hanged Ajmal Kasab (2012), Afzal Guru (2013), Yakub Memon (2015) and the Nirbhaya convicts (2020).
questions.ifAgree: The state should not kill; mistakes cannot be undone.
questions.ifDisagree: Some crimes are so terrible that only death is just.

questions.statement: Illegal immigrants should be identified and deported through a nationwide citizens’ register, as in Assam.
questions.context: Assam’s 2019 National Register of Citizens left out about 19 lakh people.
questions.ifAgree: No country can accept unlimited illegal migration.
questions.ifDisagree: Poor Indians without papers were left stateless.

questions.statement: India should never join a formal military alliance, not even with the US.
questions.context: India is in the Quad with the US, Japan and Australia, which is not a defence pact.
questions.ifAgree: Strategic autonomy has served India since Nehru.
questions.ifDisagree: China’s rise requires firm allies.

questions.statement: Farmers who burn crop stubble should be fined.
questions.context: Burning in Punjab and Haryana adds heavily to Delhi’s winter smog.
questions.ifAgree: Polluters must pay.
questions.ifDisagree: Farmers need machines and support, not penalties.

questions.statement: Foreign companies should be welcomed to make goods in India, even if they compete with Indian firms.
questions.context: Apple’s suppliers made a fast-growing share of iPhones in India by 2025 under the production-linked incentive scheme.
questions.ifAgree: Foreign factories bring jobs, skills and exports.
questions.ifDisagree: Indian champions should get first claim on incentives.

questions.statement: Free-trade agreements like the 2025 India–UK deal are good for India.
questions.context: India and the UK signed a trade agreement in July 2025 cutting tariffs on most goods.
questions.ifAgree: Cheaper inputs and new markets for textiles, leather and services.
questions.ifDisagree: Deals expose Indian farmers and small firms to foreign competition.

questions.statement: India has the right to burn coal to grow, as rich countries did.
questions.context: India’s emissions per person are less than half the world average.
questions.ifAgree: The West polluted first and must pay.
questions.ifDisagree: India suffers the worst heat waves and floods.

questions.statement: Mining and industry in forests like Hasdeo should go ahead if they create jobs.
questions.context: Villagers have protested coal mining in Chhattisgarh’s Hasdeo Arand forest since 2022.
questions.ifAgree: Mines bring royalties and jobs to poor districts.
questions.ifDisagree: Adivasi land and ancient forests should be left alone.

questions.statement: Inter-caste and interfaith couples need state protection from their own families.
questions.context: In 2018 the Supreme Court ordered safe houses and police protection to prevent honour killings.
questions.ifAgree: The safe houses ordered in Shakti Vahini v. Union of India.
questions.ifDisagree: Such matters are for families and communities.

questions.statement: The state should neither fund pilgrimages nor run religious institutions of any faith.
questions.context: States fund events like the Kumbh Mela; the Haj subsidy ended in 2018.
questions.ifAgree: A secular state keeps equal distance from all religions.
questions.ifDisagree: Supporting festivals and pilgrims is part of serving the people.

questions.statement: Comedians who mock religion or leaders deserve police cases.
questions.context: Munawar Faruqui spent over a month in jail in 2021 over jokes police could not show he had told; Kunal Kamra faced cases in 2025.
questions.ifAgree: Insulting faith or leaders crosses a line and should be punished.
questions.ifDisagree: Satire is free speech; offence is not a crime.

questions.statement: Parents should have the final say in whom their children marry.
questions.context: Most Indian marriages are arranged; surveys find only about 5% are inter-caste.
questions.ifAgree: Families know best and marriages unite families.
questions.ifDisagree: The Supreme Court has repeatedly upheld adults’ right to marry whom they choose.

questions.statement: Same-sex marriage goes against Indian culture and should not be legal.
questions.context: The Supreme Court declined to legalise it in 2023, leaving it to Parliament.
questions.ifAgree: Marriage in Indian law is between a man and a woman.
questions.ifDisagree: Gay sex was decriminalised in 2018; couples want equal rights to inherit and adopt.

questions.statement: Banning Chinese apps like TikTok after the Galwan clash was right.
questions.context: India banned 59 Chinese apps in June 2020 after 20 Indian soldiers were killed at Galwan.
questions.ifAgree: Security and data from Indian users mattered more than access.
questions.ifDisagree: Bans hurt Indian creators and users more than China.

questions.statement: Big business has too much influence over the government.
questions.context: The 2023 Hindenburg report on the Adani group, which the group denied, and the electoral-bond scheme fuelled this debate.
questions.ifAgree: The electoral-bond data released in 2024 showed large donations from companies.
questions.ifDisagree: Big Indian companies built ports, telecoms and airports the state could not.

questions.statement: India should take back Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, by force if necessary.
questions.context: Parliament resolved in 1994 that PoK is part of India.
questions.ifAgree: The 1994 resolution should be fulfilled.
questions.ifDisagree: War would cost countless lives.

questions.statement: India should spend much more on defence, even if it means less on welfare.
questions.context: India spends about 2% of GDP on defence.
questions.ifAgree: Two hostile neighbours demand a stronger military.
questions.ifDisagree: Schools and hospitals matter more.

questions.statement: Cities named after invaders should be renamed, as Allahabad became Prayagraj.
questions.context: Allahabad was renamed in 2018; Aurangabad became Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in 2023.
questions.ifAgree: Names should honour India’s own heritage.
questions.ifDisagree: Renaming erases shared history and costs money.

questions.statement: The Citizenship Amendment Act rightly fast-tracks citizenship for persecuted non-Muslim minorities from Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan.
questions.context: Passed in 2019 with rules notified in 2024; it does not cover Muslims, including persecuted sects such as Ahmadis.
questions.ifAgree: India is the natural home of minorities persecuted in Islamic neighbours.
questions.ifDisagree: Making religion a test for citizenship breaks with a secular constitution.

questions.statement: Maoist insurgents should be defeated militarily, not negotiated with.
questions.context: The government set March 2026 as its deadline to end Naxalism; the CPI (Maoist) chief Basavaraju was killed in May 2025.
questions.ifAgree: Armed groups that kill civilians and police must be crushed.
questions.ifDisagree: Talks and development address the Adivasi grievances behind the insurgency.

questions.statement: Lok Sabha and state elections should be held together, every five years.
questions.context: Bills for simultaneous elections were introduced in Parliament in December 2024.
questions.ifAgree: Less campaign spending and governments free to govern.
questions.ifDisagree: State issues would be drowned out by national ones.

questions.statement: Women should have a right to menstrual leave at work and college.
questions.context: Bihar has given government employees two days a month since 1992; Kerala gave it to university students in 2023.
questions.ifAgree: It recognises women’s health needs.
questions.ifDisagree: It may make employers less willing to hire women.

questions.statement: Hindu temples should be freed from state control and run by Hindu bodies.
questions.context: Tamil Nadu’s HR&CE department administers tens of thousands of temples; churches run their own affairs.
questions.ifAgree: Other communities run their institutions; Hindus should too.
questions.ifDisagree: State control curbed caste exclusion and misuse of temple funds.

questions.statement: The national anthem should be played before every film, with everyone standing.
questions.context: The Supreme Court made it mandatory in 2016 and optional in 2018.
questions.ifAgree: A daily reminder of national unity.
questions.ifDisagree: Patriotism cannot be compelled in a cinema hall.

questions.statement: India needs one strong leader more than coalition governments.
questions.context: No party won a majority alone from 1989 to 2014; the BJP did in 2014 and 2019 but not in 2024.
questions.ifAgree: Decisive government delivered GST, Article 370 and big infrastructure.
questions.ifDisagree: Coalitions kept power in check and passed the 1991 reforms and RTI.

questions.statement: Caste-based reservations in jobs and education should continue until caste discrimination ends.
questions.context: Reservations cover SCs, STs and OBCs within a 50% cap set by the Supreme Court in 1992, plus 10% for poorer “general” castes since 2019.
questions.ifAgree: Ambedkar argued representation was needed to undo centuries of exclusion.
questions.ifDisagree: Some argue reservations entrench caste identity and should end.

questions.statement: India should keep buying Russian oil whatever the US and Europe say.
questions.context: Russia became India’s top oil supplier after 2022; the US cited this when raising tariffs in 2025.
questions.ifAgree: India must buy energy where it is cheapest for its people.
questions.ifDisagree: It strains ties with India’s biggest trading partners.

questions.statement: English should remain the main language of courts, science and higher education.
questions.context: The Supreme Court works in English; the government promotes medicine and engineering in Indian languages.
questions.ifAgree: English connects India to the world and between states.
questions.ifDisagree: English is a colonial legacy that excludes most Indians.

questions.statement: India should sign the 1951 UN Refugee Convention.
questions.context: India is one of the largest refugee-hosting countries that has not signed it.
questions.ifAgree: Clear rules would protect refugees and India alike.
questions.ifDisagree: It would limit India’s control of its borders.

questions.statement: Amazon and Walmart’s Flipkart should not be allowed to sell their own stock to Indian shoppers, to protect kirana stores.
questions.context: Under FDI rules, foreign e-commerce firms may only run marketplaces, not sell inventory they own.
questions.ifAgree: Traders’ associations’ campaigns against “predatory pricing”.
questions.ifDisagree: Shoppers benefit from lower prices and faster delivery.

questions.statement: Opening Indian farming to world markets would help farmers more than protection.
questions.context: India keeps high duties on dairy and farm goods; dairy was a sticking point in trade talks with the US.
questions.ifAgree: Indian farmers could export more if markets opened both ways.
questions.ifDisagree: Small farmers cannot compete with subsidised Western agriculture.

questions.statement: Laws against “love jihad” and forced conversion protect Hindu women.
questions.context: Uttar Pradesh’s 2021 law requires 60 days’ notice to the district magistrate before converting for marriage.
questions.ifAgree: It stops deception and coercion.
questions.ifDisagree: It treats adult women as unable to choose and targets interfaith couples.

questions.statement: The government should guarantee a minimum support price (MSP) for all major crops by law.
questions.context: MSP is announced for 22 crops, but procurement is mostly wheat and rice; a legal guarantee was the farmers’ main demand in 2024.
questions.ifAgree: The farmer unions’ demand for a law covering every MSP crop.
questions.ifDisagree: Economists warn that guaranteed buying of every crop would strain public finances and distort planting.

questions.statement: One national entrance exam, NEET, should decide medical admissions in every state.
questions.context: Tamil Nadu passed a law in 2021 to exempt itself; the 2024 paper leak deepened the dispute.
questions.ifAgree: One merit list stops capitation-fee admissions.
questions.ifDisagree: A single exam favours students who can afford coaching.

questions.statement: Ending Article 370 and splitting Jammu and Kashmir into union territories was right.
questions.context: Done in August 2019; upheld by the Supreme Court in December 2023.
questions.ifAgree: One constitution for all of India.
questions.ifDisagree: It was done without the consent of the state’s people, under a lockdown.

questions.statement: Chinese investment should be allowed back into Indian factories if it brings jobs.
questions.context: Since April 2020, investment from countries sharing a land border with India has needed government approval.
questions.ifAgree: Electronics makers say Chinese partners and parts are hard to replace.
questions.ifDisagree: China is a strategic rival and investment brings leverage.

questions.statement: Selling Air India to the Tata group was right: governments should not run airlines.
questions.context: The state-owned airline was sold to Tata Sons in January 2022 after years of losses paid for by taxpayers.
questions.ifAgree: Supporters point to an end to bailouts and a revived airline placing record aircraft orders.
questions.ifDisagree: Critics say national assets should not be sold, and that the state can run services in the public interest.

questions.statement: Foreign universities should be welcome to open campuses in India.
questions.context: UGC rules issued in 2023 allow foreign universities to set up campuses.
questions.ifAgree: Students could get a world-class education without leaving India.
questions.ifDisagree: It would deepen inequality and drain teachers from Indian universities.

questions.statement: Being Indian is about the Constitution, not religion, language or ancestry.
questions.context: The Constitution’s preamble speaks of a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.
questions.ifAgree: India is a civic nation of many faiths and languages.
questions.ifDisagree: India is a civilisation rooted in Hindu culture.

questions.statement: Muslims face real discrimination in housing and jobs, and the law should address it.
questions.context: The Sachar Committee (2006) found Muslims behind in education and jobs; Muslims are about 14% of the population.
questions.ifAgree: An anti-discrimination law covering private housing.
questions.ifDisagree: Special measures amount to “appeasement”.

questions.statement: Building the Ram temple at Ayodhya was a national achievement.
questions.context: The Supreme Court awarded the site in 2019; the Prime Minister led the consecration in January 2024.
questions.ifAgree: It ended a centuries-old dispute and fulfilled a long-held faith.
questions.ifDisagree: The state should not lead a religious ceremony.

questions.statement: Hindi should be promoted as the link language across India.
questions.context: The 2020 education policy’s three-language formula is resisted by Tamil Nadu, which follows a two-language policy.
questions.ifAgree: A shared language binds a nation.
questions.ifDisagree: The 1965 anti-Hindi agitation in Tamil Nadu showed imposition divides India.

questions.statement: The Supreme Court was right to strike down electoral bonds as secret political funding.
questions.context: In February 2024 the court ended the scheme; the data showed the BJP received the largest share.
questions.ifAgree: Voters have a right to know who funds parties.
questions.ifDisagree: Bonds moved donations into the banking system.

questions.statement: The Old Pension Scheme should not come back; guaranteed pensions for government staff are unaffordable.
questions.context: Several states returned to the Old Pension Scheme; the centre introduced the Unified Pension Scheme in 2024.
questions.ifAgree: Economists warn pension bills crowd out schools and roads.
questions.ifDisagree: Unions say employees deserve secure retirement income.

questions.statement: The government should cap prices of essentials like onions and medicines when they rise sharply.
questions.context: India bans or limits onion exports when prices spike and caps prices of essential drugs under the Drugs Price Control Order.
questions.ifAgree: The price caps on cardiac stents and knee implants (2017).
questions.ifDisagree: Export bans hurt farmers just when prices are good for them.

questions.statement: Loss-making public companies such as BSNL should be privatised, not revived with public money.
questions.context: BSNL has received several government revival packages since 2019.
questions.ifAgree: The sale of Air India or the listing of LIC.
questions.ifDisagree: Keeping BSNL as a state carrier to serve remote areas.

questions.statement: Cow slaughter should be banned in every state.
questions.context: Most states ban it; Kerala, West Bengal and several north-eastern states do not.
questions.ifAgree: The cow is sacred to many Hindus.
questions.ifDisagree: Diet is a personal choice; lynchings by cow vigilantes show the danger.

questions.statement: The strikes on Pakistan in Operation Sindoor were the right response to the Pahalgam attack.
questions.context: After 26 people were killed at Pahalgam in April 2025, India struck targets in Pakistan on 7 May; four days of fighting followed.
questions.ifAgree: Terror must carry a military cost.
questions.ifDisagree: Strikes risk a war between nuclear powers.

questions.statement: Police “encounter” killings of dreaded criminals are acceptable when courts are too slow.
questions.context: Uttar Pradesh police said in 2023 that 183 suspects had been killed in encounters since 2017.
questions.ifAgree: Gangsters feared the state and crime fell, supporters say.
questions.ifDisagree: Extrajudicial killing is murder by the state, whoever the victim.

questions.statement: Jammu and Kashmir’s full statehood should be restored now.
questions.context: Promised since 2019; Omar Abdullah’s elected government took office in 2024 with the limited powers of a union territory.
questions.ifAgree: An elected government should have the powers of a state.
questions.ifDisagree: Security conditions come first.

questions.statement: Drug use by adults, like the bhang sold legally in some states, should not be a crime.
questions.context: The NDPS Act punishes possession; Aryan Khan was arrested in 2021 and the case against him was dropped in 2022.
questions.ifAgree: Addiction is a health problem, and jail destroys lives.
questions.ifDisagree: Punjab’s drug crisis shows the need for tough laws.

questions.statement: Monthly cash for women, like Ladli Behna or Lakshmir Bhandar, is good policy, not a bribe for votes.
questions.context: Madhya Pradesh (2023), West Bengal (2021), Maharashtra (2024) and other states pay women ₹1,000–2,500 a month.
questions.ifAgree: It gives women money of their own and was copied by parties of every colour.
questions.ifDisagree: Critics say schemes announced before elections strain budgets.

questions.statement: Redrawing Lok Sabha seats should not cut the share of southern states that slowed their population growth.
questions.context: Seat numbers have been frozen on 1971 census figures; the freeze ends after the first census taken after 2026.
questions.ifAgree: States should not be punished for successful family planning.
questions.ifDisagree: One person, one vote means seats should follow population.

questions.statement: Rape within marriage should not be a crime; the law would be misused and harm families.
questions.context: The 2023 penal code keeps an exception for husbands; challenges are pending in the Supreme Court.
questions.ifAgree: The central government told the Supreme Court in 2024 that criminalising it would be excessively harsh and is a social question.
questions.ifDisagree: Most countries now treat rape within marriage as a crime.

questions.statement: Police should need a court warrant to tap phones, and spyware like Pegasus should be banned.
questions.context: A Supreme Court committee examined Pegasus spyware allegations in 2021–22.
questions.ifAgree: The Supreme Court recognised privacy as a fundamental right in 2017.
questions.ifDisagree: Security agencies need surveillance tools against terror.

questions.statement: Demonetisation showed decisive leadership, even if it caused hardship.
questions.context: On 8 November 2016 ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes were withdrawn overnight; the RBI later said 99.3% came back.
questions.ifAgree: It pushed digital payments like UPI and hit black money.
questions.ifDisagree: Queues, lost jobs in the informal economy and little black money caught.

trivia: India’s Constitution, which came into force on 26 January 1950, is the longest written national constitution in the world.
The 2024 general election had about 97 crore registered voters, the largest electorate ever.
The words “socialist” and “secular” were added to the preamble by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, during the Emergency.
Universal adult suffrage applied from India’s first general election in 1951–52.
The anti-defection law was added to the Constitution in 1985.
The Right to Information Act of 2005 lets any citizen demand government records within 30 days.
The Supreme Court’s Kesavananda Bharati judgement (1973) held that Parliament cannot change the Constitution’s basic structure.
The Mandal Commission’s OBC reservation was implemented in 1990 and upheld in 1992 with a 50% cap.
UPI processed more than 18 billion payments a month in 2025.
India’s Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats, frozen on the 1971 census until after the first census taken after 2026.
The Supreme Court decriminalised homosexuality in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, 2018.
Privacy was declared a fundamental right in Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017.
The 73rd Amendment (1992) reserved one-third of panchayat seats for women; many states now reserve half.
The first non-Congress government at the centre was the Janata Party’s, in 1977.
Tamil Nadu’s 69% reservation is protected by the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.
The Emergency lasted 21 months, from June 1975 to March 1977.
